claim: An engineered split mNeonGreen protein was used to generate a large-scale endogenous tag library in HEK293 cells.
source: Recently, an engineered split mNeonGreen protein was used to generate a large-scale endogenous tag library in HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references the OpenCell project mentioned later in the manuscript.

claim: The smNG2-P cell line enables fast and efficient endogenous tagging of proteins with the short fragment mNG211.
source: We engineered an iPS cell line to express the large fragment of the split mNeonGreen protein (mNG21-10) and showed that it enables fast and efficient endogenous tagging of proteins with the short fragment (mNG211).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the manuscript with multiple tagged proteins.

claim: Neural network-based image restoration enables live imaging studies of highly dynamic cellular processes such as cytokinesis in iPSCs.
source: We also demonstrate that neural network-based image restoration enables live imaging studies of highly dynamic cellular processes such as cytokinesis in iPSCs.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4 and Figure 5 where CARE neural network is used to restore images of cytokinesis.

claim: GFP was first described as a fluorescent reporter by Chalfie et al., 1994.
source: Since GFP was first described as a fluorescent reporter (Chalfie et al., 1994), the use of fluorescent proteins has become a standard method to study the localization and function of proteins inside living cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chalfie et al., 1994.

claim: Over-expression from exogenous plasmids can induce artifacts of localization and protein-protein interactions.
source: Further, over-expression can induce artifacts of localization and protein-protein interactions, making data challenging to interpret (Gibson et al., 2013; Mahen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gibson et al., 2013 and Mahen et al., 2014.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 can be used to introduce a double-stranded break at a target site for homology-directed repair.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 is used to introduce a double-stranded break at the target site, which can be repaired by homology-directed repair (HDR) using a repair template carrying the fluorescent marker (Verma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Verma et al., 2017 and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Endogenous tagging enables the study of proteins at endogenous expression levels and provides more reliable measurements of protein behavior.
source: This enables the study of proteins at endogenous expression levels and provides more reliable measurements of protein behavior (Dambournet et al., 2018; Doyon et al., 2011; Husser et al., 2022; Mahen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Dambournet et al., 2018; Doyon et al., 2011; Husser et al., 2022; Mahen et al., 2014.

claim: Whole-genome libraries of endogenous tags have been generated in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: Endogenous tagging is commonly done in model organisms such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae, for which whole-genome libraries of endogenous tags have been generated (Huh et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Huh et al., 2003.

claim: Gene editing in human cells is less widely used than in model organisms due to limitations in efficiency caused by transfection and HDR.
source: However, gene editing in human cells is less widely used due to limitations in efficiency caused by transfection and HDR, among other issues.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field based on general knowledge.

claim: The majority of human proteins have not been tagged and studied at the endogenous level.
source: Because of these bottlenecks, the majority of human proteins have not been tagged and studied at the endogenous level.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations described and the context of the field.

claim: The split mNeonGreen system consists of a large fragment (mNG21-10) composed of the first ten beta-strands and a short fragment (mNG211) corresponding to the eleventh beta strand.
source: In the split mNeonGreen system, the mNeonGreen protein is expressed as two separate fragments: a large fragment composed of the first ten beta-strands of mNeonGreen (mNG21-10) and a short fragment corresponding to the eleventh beta strand (mNG211; Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Feng et al., 2017 and describes the technical design of the system.

claim: The two fragments of split mNeonGreen have been engineered to form a functional fluorescent protein when co-expressed.
source: The two fragments have been engineered to form a functional fluorescent protein when co-expressed (Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Feng et al., 2017.

claim: The interaction between mNG21-10 and mNG211 is characterized by high complementation efficiency and is irreversible once the reconstituted protein has folded.
source: This interaction is characterized by a high complementation efficiency and is irreversible once the reconstituted protein has folded (Feng et al., 2019; Köker et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Feng et al., 2019 and Köker et al., 2018.

claim: The split mNeonGreen2 protein retains most of the brightness of the original mNeonGreen.
source: Moreover, the split mNeonGreen2 protein retains most of the brightness of the original mNeonGreen (Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Feng et al., 2017.

claim: The mNG211 fragment is only 16 amino acids long.
source: The mNG211 fragment is only 16 amino acids long, so it can be inserted into the genome by HDR using a repair template with short homology arms (generally 40–80 bp), which can be purchased commercially as a single-stranded oligo-deoxynucleotide (ssODN).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the size of the mNG211 fragment.

claim: Large-scale endogenous tagging in HEK293 cells was achieved by the OpenCell project, with 1310 proteins tagged.
source: Large-scale endogenous tagging in HEK293 cells was recently achieved by the OpenCell project, with 1310 proteins tagged to date (Cho et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cho et al., 2022.

claim: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were discovered in 2007.
source: Since their discovery in 2007, human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have become a popular tool to study human cells in developmental contexts and to identify disease-causing mutations, amongst other valuable applications (Shi et al., 2017; Takahashi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Shi et al., 2017 and Takahashi et al., 2007.

claim: iPSCs are derived from somatic cells that are reprogrammed to be self-renewing and pluripotent.
source: iPSCs are derived from somatic cells that are reprogrammed to be self-renewing and pluripotent.
evidence: This is established knowledge about iPSCs.

claim: iPSCs can be cultured and differentiated into any desired cell type in vitro using specific protocols.
source: These cells can be cultured and differentiated into any desired cell type in vitro using specific protocols (e.g. Grancharova et al., 2021; Hong and Do, 2019; Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grancharova et al., 2021; Hong and Do, 2019; Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2022.

claim: Few studies have investigated cellular processes in human stem cells and differentiated cell types with high spatiotemporal resolution.
source: Despite this incredible resource, few studies have investigated cellular processes in human stem cells and differentiated cell types with high spatiotemporal resolution (Dambournet et al., 2018; Viana et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dambournet et al., 2018 and Viana et al., 2023, and represents an assessment of the current state of the field.

claim: Most knowledge of human cell cytokinesis is derived from diseased and/or transformed cell lines.
source: Since most of our knowledge of human cell cytokinesis is derived from diseased and/or transformed cell lines, the field will benefit greatly from studying iPSCs before and after differentiation in an isogenic context, particularly since they represent 'healthy' human cells (Dambournet et al., 2018; Drubin and Hyman, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dambournet et al., 2018 and Drubin and Hyman, 2017.

claim: The smNG2-P cell line was generated by integrating an mNG21-10 expression cassette at the AAVS1 locus in 201B7 iPSCs.
source: First, we engineered a human iPS cell line that constitutively expresses the mNG21-10 fragment. We validated this cell line extensively and named it 'smNG2-P' (split mNeonGreen2 parental cell line).
evidence: This is a primary finding described in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Multiple genes were efficiently targeted for endogenous tagging with mNG211 in the smNG2-P cell line.
source: As a proof-of-concept, we efficiently targeted multiple genes for endogenous tagging with mNG211, and clonally isolated several tagged iPS cell lines.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated in Figure 2 and Figure 3.

claim: Protocols were developed for efficient single-cell isolation by FACS and screening of edited clones by Nanopore sequencing.
source: To facilitate this process, we developed protocols for efficient single-cell isolation by FACS (fluorescence-activated cell sorting) and screening of edited clones by Nanopore sequencing.
evidence: This is described in the methods and results sections, particularly in Figure 3.

claim: The mNG21-10 expression cassette contains the CAG promoter to drive high levels of expression and resist silencing at the AAVS1 locus.
source: This cassette contains the CAG promoter to drive high levels of mNG21-10 expression, and resist silencing at the AAVS1 locus over time and during differentiation (Luo et al., 2014; Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Luo et al., 2014 and Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2016.

claim: The 201B7 cell line was generated by retroviral transduction of reprogramming factors into dermal fibroblasts.
source: We introduced this mNG21-10 expression cassette into the 201B7 cell line, which was generated by retroviral transduction of reprogramming factors into dermal fibroblasts and is well-characterized (Takahashi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Takahashi et al., 2007.

claim: Six clones were found to be heterozygous for AAVS1-mNG21-10 integration after screening.
source: We found 6 clones that were heterozygous for AAVS1-mNG21-10 integration, and one clone was selected for full validation (clone 28).
evidence: This is a result from the screening process described in the manuscript.

claim: Sequencing of the AAVS1 locus in clone 28 revealed that one allele contains the mNG21-10 expression cassette while the other allele is unedited.
source: Sequencing of the AAVS1 locus revealed that one allele contains the mNG21-10 expression cassette, while the other allele is unedited (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C with sequencing chromatograms.

claim: Digital PCR confirmed the presence of a single copy of mNG21-10 with no ectopic integration in clone 28.
source: Our data confirmed the presence of a single copy of mNG21-10 with no ectopic integration (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A with digital PCR data.

claim: No differences were found in the sequence of 12 off-target sites between the WT 201B7 cell line and clone 28 cells.
source: We found no differences in the sequence of the 12 off-target sites between the WT 201B7 cell line and our edited cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–M).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–M with sequencing data.

claim: Clone 28 cells have a normal karyotype (46, XX).
source: To ensure that the clone 28 cells have a normal genome, we performed G-banding karyotyping and found no chromosomal abnormalities (46, XX karyotype; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D with karyotype analysis.

claim: Clone 28 cells express the pluripotency markers TRA-1–60, OCT3/4, and NANOG.
source: To verify that clone 28 cells are undifferentiated, we used immunofluorescence staining and flow cytometry with antibodies specific for TRA-1–60, OCT3/4, and NANOG (Figure 1E). We found that all three pluripotency markers were expressed.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E with flow cytometry data.

claim: Clone 28 cells retain pluripotency by successfully differentiating into ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
source: We also found that clone 28 cells retain pluripotency by successfully differentiating them into ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm, as determined by immunofluorescence staining and flow cytometry with antibodies specific for PAX6 (ectoderm), NCAM (mesoderm), and FOXA2 (endoderm; Figure 1F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F with flow cytometry data.

claim: Clone 28 cells tested negative for mycoplasma contamination.
source: Clone 28 cells also have normal iPSC morphology and tested negative for mycoplasma contamination (Figure 1—figure supplement 2N–O).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2N–O.

claim: Transfection of clone 28 cells with a plasmid expressing H2B fused to mNG11 resulted in fluorescent signal localized to chromatin.
source: Transfection of clone 28 cells with a plasmid expressing H2B (histone) fused to the mNG11 fragment resulted in the expression of a fluorescent signal localized to chromatin as expected for the functional complementation of the mNG21-10 and mNG211 fragments (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1G with fluorescence microscopy images.

claim: 17 genes were selected for endogenous tagging with mNG211.
source: We selected 17 genes for tagging, some of which had been previously endogenously tagged with the split mNG system (e.g. ACTB, TUBA1B, KRT18; Cho et al., 2022) or with full-length fluorescent proteins (e.g. H2BC11, ACTB, ANLN, RHOA; Husser et al., 2022; Roberts et al., 2017), while other genes had not been tagged previously (e.g. RACGAP1, KRT5, TUBB3, FOXA2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cas9 targeting was efficient for all loci tested, as shown by the high proportion of indels in edited cell populations.
source: We found that Cas9 targeting was efficient for all loci, as shown by the high proportion of indels in the edited cell populations.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The proportion of tagged alleles varied considerably for each locus, ranging from 0.69% to 37.5%.
source: However, the proportion of tagged alleles was variable, with 37.5% of CDH1 alleles tagged, while only 0.69% of TUBA1B alleles were tagged (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B with Nanopore sequencing data.

claim: Fluorescent signal was observed in H2BC11, ACTB, TUBA1B, ANLN, RHOA, KRT18, SOX2, NES, and TUBB3-tagged populations.
source: As expected for genes that are expressed in iPSCs, we observed a fluorescent signal in H2BC11, ACTB, TUBA1B, ANLN, RHOA, KRT18, SOX2, NES, and TUBB3-tagged populations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–T).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–T with flow cytometry data.

claim: The mean fluorescence intensity of tagged cells correlated well with their expected relative expression levels.
source: For these proteins, the mean fluorescence intensity of tagged cells correlated well with their expected relative expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and U).
evidence: This is shown by comparing Figure 2—figure supplement 1A (RNA-seq data) and Figure 2—figure supplement 1U (fluorescence intensity).

claim: E-cadherin-mNG211 was enriched at cell junctions.
source: However, microscopy revealed that E-cadherin-mNG211 was enriched at cell junctions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1V; Allencell.org; Aban et al., 2021; Cumin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1V with microscopy images and supported by citations.

claim: No fluorescent signal was observed from tagged Cyk4 (RACGAP1 gene) by flow cytometry or microscopy.
source: However, we did not observe any fluorescent signal from tagged Cyk4 (RACGAP1 gene) by flow cytometry or microscopy (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Nuclear fluorescence was observed in FOXA2-tagged cells after induction into endoderm.
source: We observed nuclear fluorescence by microscopy in FOXA2-tagged cells after induction into endoderm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1W–X), but we did not investigate the expression of the others as this goes beyond the scope of our study.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1W–X with microscopy images.

claim: An average recovery of 61.4% was achieved for single-cell clones in 96-well plates across five genes.
source: We optimized a protocol to efficiently recover single-cell clones after FACS (shown in Figure 3A), resulting in an average recovery of 61.4% in 96-well plates across the five genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A with recovery rate data.

claim: Isolated clones had diverse genotypes with alleles containing mNG211, mutated mNG211, indel mutations, and WT sequences.
source: We found that clones had diverse genotypes with alleles containing mNG211, mutated mNG211, indel mutations, and WT sequences (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B with genotyping data from Nanopore sequencing.

claim: Both homozygous and heterozygous clones were obtained for smNG2-anillin and smNG2-RhoA.
source: We obtained both homozygous and heterozygous clones carrying smNG2-anillin and smNG2-RhoA, and we found homozygous clones that were brighter than heterozygous ones (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I with fluorescence intensity measurements.

claim: Homozygous clones for anillin and RhoA were brighter than heterozygous clones.
source: We obtained both homozygous and heterozygous clones carrying smNG2-anillin and smNG2-RhoA, and we found homozygous clones that were brighter than heterozygous ones (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I with fluorescence intensity measurements.

claim: The complementation between mNG21-10 and mNG211 occurs efficiently over a range of mNG211 expression levels.
source: This suggests that the complementation between mNG21-10 and mNG211 occurs efficiently over a range of mNG211 expression, since anillin is expressed weakly and RhoA is expressed more strongly in iPSCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both weakly and strongly expressed proteins show efficient complementation.

claim: H2B was nuclear during interphase and localized to condensed chromatin during mitosis in the final tagged cell lines.
source: Consistent with the expected localization for these proteins, H2B was nuclear during interphase and localized to condensed chromatin during mitosis, actin was cortical in both interphase and mitotic cells, tubulin was cytosolic during interphase and localized to mitotic spindles, anillin was nuclear during interphase and enriched in the cleavage furrow during cytokinesis, and RhoA was cytosolic during interphase and cortically enriched during mitosis.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3H with microscopy images.

claim: iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip after a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings.
source: After a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings, iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip, independently of laser wavelength (data not shown), suggesting that iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.
evidence: This is an observation made during live imaging experiments.

claim: iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.
source: After a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings, iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip, independently of laser wavelength (data not shown), suggesting that iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that iPSCs stopped dividing during imaging.

claim: The signal-to-noise ratio was low for H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA in images acquired with low-exposure settings.
source: Indeed, the signal-to-noise ratio was low for H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA in images acquired with low-exposure settings that supported cell survival, compared to images acquired using high-exposure settings that did not support cell viability (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A with signal-to-noise ratio measurements.

claim: A CARE neural network was trained on sets of matched high- and low-exposure images for each cell line.
source: We trained a CARE (Content-Aware image REstoration) neural network on sets of matched high- and low-exposure images for each cell line (Figure 4B; Weigert et al., 2018), and used the trained model to restore timelapse movies acquired with low-exposure settings (Figure 4C–G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B and described in the methods section.

claim: The signal-to-noise ratio was drastically improved for timelapse images of H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA after CARE restoration.
source: The signal-to-noise ratio was drastically improved for timelapse images of H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA (Figure 4C–G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C–G with comparisons of raw and restored images.

claim: The duration of contractile ring ingression in anillin-tagged iPSCs is 18.6±4.0 min.
source: First we measured the duration of contractile ring ingression in anillin-tagged iPSCs (18.6±4.0 min; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B with timing measurements.

claim: In metaphase iPSCs, anillin is cytosolic, RhoA is weakly enriched at the cortex, and actin is strongly enriched at the cortex.
source: In metaphase cells, we found that anillin is cytosolic, while RhoA is weakly enriched at the cortex and actin is strongly enriched at the cortex (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5C).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4C, D, G and 5C with microscopy images and measurements.

claim: Anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset in iPSCs.
source: During mitotic exit, anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset, while RhoA accumulates by ~6 min, and actin remains strongly cortical with some equatorial enrichment by ~4–5 min (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5D).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4C, D, G and 5D with timelapse imaging data.

claim: RhoA accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~6 min after anaphase onset in iPSCs.
source: During mitotic exit, anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset, while RhoA accumulates by ~6 min, and actin remains strongly cortical with some equatorial enrichment by ~4–5 min (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5D).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 4C, D, G and 5D with timelapse imaging data.

claim: Anillin forms a narrow peak at the onset of ingression (4.1±0.7 μm) in iPSCs.
source: We then measured the breadth of cortically enriched anillin and RhoA at the onset of ingression and found that anillin forms a narrow peak (4.1±0.7 μm), while RhoA localizes more broadly (6.6±2.2 μm; Figure 5E–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5E–F with breadth measurements.

claim: RhoA localizes more broadly at the onset of ingression (6.6±2.2 μm) compared to anillin in iPSCs.
source: We then measured the breadth of cortically enriched anillin and RhoA at the onset of ingression and found that anillin forms a narrow peak (4.1±0.7 μm), while RhoA localizes more broadly (6.6±2.2 μm; Figure 5E–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5E–F with breadth measurements.

claim: iPSCs have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase.
source: We found that cells have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase (Figure 5G–H), and the astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G–H with microscopy images and intensity measurements.

claim: Astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex in iPSCs during anaphase.
source: We found that cells have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase (Figure 5G–H), and the astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G with microscopy images.

claim: Anillin-tagged iPSCs completed ingression faster than HepG2 and HEK293 cells, slower than HCT116 cells, and similar to HeLa cells.
source: We found that anillin-tagged iPSCs completed ingression in 18.6±4.0 min; faster than HepG2 and HEK293 cells, slower than HCT116 cells, and similar to HeLa cells (Figure 5B; Husser et al., 2022).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B and compared to data from Husser et al., 2022.

claim: The weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA.
source: Thus, the weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the weak central spindle and broad RhoA localization.

claim: Perturbations that weaken the central spindle in HeLa cells result in more diffuse Ect2-Cyk4 complexes and a broader zone of active RhoA.
source: In support of this, perturbations that weaken the central spindle in HeLa cells result in more diffuse Ect2-Cyk4 complexes and a broader zone of active RhoA (Adriaans et al., 2019; Kotýnková et al., 2016; Su et al., 2011; Yüce et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Adriaans et al., 2019; Kotýnková et al., 2016; Su et al., 2011; Yüce et al., 2005.

claim: The 201B7 smNG2-P cell line is heterozygous for the mNG21-10 expression cassette integrated at the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus.
source: The 201B7 smNG2-P cell line is heterozygous for the mNG21-10 expression cassette which was integrated at the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in the results.

claim: Integration at the AAVS1 locus minimizes the risk of mNG21-10 silencing and provides high and consistent expression across all cells.
source: Compared to lentiviral delivery, this design minimizes the risk of mNG21-10 silencing and provides a high and consistent expression of mNG21-10 across all cells in the population, even over time and during differentiation (Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2016.

claim: Tagging efficiency with mNG211 in iPSCs ranged from 0.69% to 37.5%.
source: We tagged multiple genes with mNG211, with efficiencies ranging from 0.69% to 37.5% measured by Nanopore sequencing (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B with Nanopore sequencing data.

claim: Tagging efficiency with mNG211 in iPSCs was lower than in mouse embryos (40 to 100% of injected embryos).
source: Tagging efficiency with mNG211 in iPSCs was lower than in mouse embryos (40 to 100% of injected embryos; O'Hagan et al., 2021), and lower than tagging with GFP11 in HEK293 cells (<1 to 56% tagged alleles; Cho et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a comparison to data from O'Hagan et al., 2021 and Cho et al., 2022.

claim: Endogenous tagging with mNG211 was overall more efficient than endogenous tagging with full-length mEGFP in iPSCs.
source: However, endogenous tagging with mNG211 was overall more efficient than endogenous tagging with full-length mEGFP in iPSCs (mostly <0.1 to 4%, and up to 24% GFP-positive cells; Roberts et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to data from Roberts et al., 2017.

claim: Low endogenous expression levels can limit the detection of tagged proteins by flow cytometry.
source: We also found that low endogenous expression levels can limit the detection of tagged proteins by flow cytometry, similar to previous studies (Cho et al., 2022; Leonetti et al., 2016; O'Hagan et al., 2021), requiring microscopy with highly sensitive cameras or detectors.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2022; Leonetti et al., 2016; O'Hagan et al., 2021.

claim: The expression levels of 9 mNG211-tagged proteins in iPSCs were consistent with RNA-seq data.
source: Importantly, the expression levels of 9 mNG211-tagged proteins in iPSCs (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1U) were consistent with RNA-seq data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Iwasaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This is shown by comparing Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1U, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A with RNA-seq data from Iwasaki et al., 2022.

claim: It is unlikely that the mNG211 tag affected the function of the tagged proteins since they showed unique localization patterns consistent with their function.
source: Since these proteins showed unique localizations patterns consistent with their function, it is unlikely that the mNG211 tag affected their function.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tagged proteins localized as expected.

claim: Nestin and β–3-tubulin were expressed at low levels in undifferentiated iPSCs despite being commonly used as differentiation markers.
source: Interestingly, Nestin and β–3-tubulin were expressed at low levels in undifferentiated iPSCs, despite being commonly used as ectodermal and neuronal differentiation markers.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The expression of Nestin and β–3-tubulin in some iPS cell lines is consistent with previous reports and published RNA-seq and proteomic data for the 201B7 cell line.
source: This result is consistent with a previous report of their expression in some iPS cell lines (Kuang et al., 2019) and with published RNA-seq and proteomic data for the 201B7 cell line (Iwasaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kuang et al., 2019 and Iwasaki et al., 2022.

claim: Edited cells had diverse genotypes caused by gene editing, including alleles carrying mutated mNG211 tags and indel mutations.
source: We also found that edited cells had diverse genotypes caused by gene editing, including alleles carrying mutated mNG211 tags and indel mutations, warranting clonal isolation.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B with genotyping data.

claim: Single-nucleotide mutations may come from mutations introduced during ssODN synthesis.
source: Single-nucleotide mutations may come from mutations introduced during ssODN synthesis.
evidence: This is speculation about the source of mutations observed.

claim: ssODN re-arrangements could be caused by microhomologies, repair by NHEJ instead of HDR, or a combination of NHEJ and HDR repair.
source: Meanwhile, ssODN re-arrangements could be caused by microhomologies, repair by NHEJ instead of HDR, or a combination of NHEJ and HDR repair (Skryabin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Skryabin et al., 2020.

claim: Clonal isolation provides a more reliable readout of protein expression where variations in signal between cells represent true cell-to-cell variability.
source: Unwanted editing outcomes are ignored when looking at pooled populations, and we recommend isolating and screening clonal cell lines to perform quantitative studies of desired cellular processes, as they provide a more reliable readout of protein expression, where variations in signal between cells within a population represent true cell-to-cell variability.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the observation of diverse genotypes in edited populations.

claim: iPSCs are programmed to undergo dissociation-induced apoptosis upon loss of attachment or cell-cell contact.
source: Clonal isolation is notoriously inefficient in iPSCs, which are programmed to undergo dissociation-induced apoptosis upon loss of attachment or cell-cell contact (Bhargava et al., 2022; Chen and Pruett-Miller, 2018; Singh, 2019; Tristan et al., 2023; Watanabe et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bhargava et al., 2022; Chen and Pruett-Miller, 2018; Singh, 2019; Tristan et al., 2023; Watanabe et al., 2007.

claim: Up to 80% of wells in a 96-well plate showed clonal growth after 10 days using the optimized protocol.
source: We optimized a protocol for efficient single-cell recovery of 201B7 iPSCs after FACS, with up to 80% of wells in a 96-well plate showing clonal growth after 10 days (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: mNG21-10/mNG211 complementation is comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins in terms of fluorescence stability and range of expression levels.
source: After clonal isolation, we found that the cells in each edited line had consistent, stable fluorescence. Further, we observed different levels of fluorescence across a range of protein expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–T), showing that mNG21-10/mNG211 complementation is comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of stable fluorescence across different expression levels.

claim: The stability of fluorescence levels in endogenously tagged cell lines and the absence of localization artifacts makes this system attractive for quantitative measurements in live cells.
source: Importantly, the stability of fluorescence levels in endogenously tagged cell lines and the absence of localization artifacts compared to over-expressed transgenes makes this system attractive for quantitative measurements in live cells (Husser et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Husser et al., 2022.

claim: iPSCs are particularly sensitive to phototoxicity compared to other cell types.
source: We found that iPSCs are particularly sensitive to phototoxicity, making it difficult to image weakly expressed endogenous tags over longer periods of time or with short time intervals.
evidence: This is an observation from live imaging experiments.

claim: The sensitivity of iPSCs to phototoxicity has not been previously reported in human or mouse stem cells.
source: This sensitivity has not been previously reported in human or in mouse stem cells, likely because imaging conditions are rarely reported and vary with different setups.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of reports in the literature.

claim: CARE allows cells to be imaged over extended periods of time with high temporal resolution using low exposure settings.
source: With this network, cells can be imaged over extended periods of time with high temporal resolution using low exposure settings, and image files can be restored to generate high-quality movies (Figure 4 and Figure 4—videos 1–6).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4 with comparisons of raw and restored images.

claim: Cytokinesis in live human iPSCs was characterized for the first time in this study.
source: As a proof-of-concept, we characterized cytokinesis in live human iPSCs for the first time.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the manuscript.

claim: Most knowledge of human cell cytokinesis was obtained from studies using HeLa cells.
source: Most of our knowledge of human cell cytokinesis was obtained from studies using HeLa cells, yet the mechanisms regulating this process are expected to vary with cell type (Husser et al., 2022; Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Husser et al., 2022 and Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022.

claim: The weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA compared to HeLa cells.
source: In HeLa cells, the central spindle starts to form immediately after anaphase onset and reaches the cortex by late anaphase (~6 min) (van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014). Thus, the weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to HeLa cells and supported by a citation to van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014.

claim: Astral microtubules extending to the cortex in the equatorial region could restrict anillin localization in iPSCs.
source: In iPSCs, the astral microtubules extended to the cortex in the equatorial region, which could restrict anillin localization.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of astral microtubules and narrow anillin localization.

claim: Perturbations that cause an increase in astral microtubules decrease the breadth of anillin in HeLa cells.
source: In HeLa cells, we previously showed that perturbations that cause an increase in astral microtubules decreases the breadth of anillin (van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014.

claim: Interactions with other proteins or phospholipids could further restrict the localization of anillin in iPSCs.
source: However, interactions with other proteins or phospholipids could further restrict the localization of anillin in iPSCs (Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022).
evidence: This is speculation supported by a citation to Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022.

claim: The findings reveal how cytokinesis occurs in a non-transformed human stem cell and provide a framework to reveal how mechanisms vary with different cell types.
source: Thus our findings reveal how cytokinesis occurs in a non-transformed human stem cell, and provide a framework to reveal how the mechanisms controlling cytokinesis vary with different cell types in an isogenic context.
evidence: This is a summary of the significance of the findings.

claim: High transfection and editing efficiencies can be achieved in iPSCs by using electroporation and delivering Cas9/sgRNA RNP complexes instead of plasmids.
source: High transfection and editing efficiencies can be achieved in iPSCs by using electroporation and delivering Cas9/sgRNA RNP complexes instead of plasmids (Kim et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2014 and Liang et al., 2015.

claim: Tagging efficiency is increased by using NHEJ inhibitors.
source: Tagging efficiency is further increased by using NHEJ inhibitors (Chu et al., 2015; Maruyama et al., 2015; Maurissen and Woltjen, 2020; Schimmel et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chu et al., 2015; Maruyama et al., 2015; Maurissen and Woltjen, 2020; Schimmel et al., 2023.

claim: This work provides the basis for a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs.
source: Altogether, this work provides the basis for a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs, which will be used to study protein function in human stem cells and across human cell types in vitro.
evidence: This is a summary of the significance and future applications of the work.
